main_body: Timber-framed farm building: a large red tile roof with a dormer on top, and a plaster-and-timber front wall with a big double barn door below
top_band: Tile roof slope, rows 3-53 at x=47: cream ridge highlight (rows 3-4), then orange, red and purple tile rows. It is one large sloped surface, with a dormer on it.
evidence: The roof is a tall tiled slope with a ridge highlight and a dormer, ending in a dark eave-shadow row at rows 54-55. Below it is a separate vertical wall of about 35 rows with timber posts and beams, windows with sills, and a framed double door. This is the same roof-over-wall structure the Beodeul house references use. There is no receding side face, and the top and front are both clearly drawn.

style.evidence: The roof tiles carry per-tile highlights in 4-5 tones, and the plaster is speckled. The door planks, timber braces and windows are shaded with several browns. The measured facts back this up: 21 colours per tile against the references' 18 and 11, 0% flat-fill coverage, and only 1% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines are tinted brown or purple rather than black. At the same scale it matches the references and does not look thinner or flatter.
